To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
novelty, and not the aversive operant escape learning, enhanced the IEG expression in the mPFc, CA1, and DG areas of rats.
novelty, but not operantly learned aversive escape behavior, enhances Fos expression in the mPC and CA1, and enhances Egr-1 in mPC and DG of rats.
novelty, and not operant aversion learning, enhances IEG expression in the prefrontal and limbic structures of rats.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of IEGs in learning and memory processes.
the role played by the mPFC, CA1, and DG in the processing of novelty, and in the learning of aversive events.
the role of the medial prefronto-hippocampal circuit on the detection of novel stimuli and the processing of aversive events.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pattern of FOS and EGR-1 expression in prefrontal and limbic areas is not only experience-dependent, but it is also dependent on the type of experience.
novelty, not learning, induces IEG expression in the mPC, CA1 and DG.
IEGs are not only activated in response to stressful events, but also to the perception of novelty, and that this activation may be experience dependent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mPFC is more involved in the detection of novelty than in the operant aversion learning.
the mPFC, CA1, and DG are involved in the detection of new events, and the IEG expression pattern may reflect the degree of novelty.
novelty, but not operantly learned aversive stimuli, enhances Fos expression in the mPC and CA1, and Egr- 1 in the mPC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the IEG expression is experience-dependent and that novelty is a relevant variable in studies on FOS and EGR-1.
a previous exposure to inescapability may not be the best control for a novel stimulus.
the expression of immediate early genes (IEGs) is not a reliable marker for learning in the aversive context, and it should be used cautiously.
